phase_note: TASKS GENERATED 2026-08-01 against the 11-requirement / 76-criterion requirements.md and the Req-11 design. DESIGN APPROVED by the maintainer at the start of this run, in answer to the gate this skill enforces, and TASKS APPROVED by the maintainer at the end of it, so ready_for_implementation is true. SHAPE: 8 majors, 38 sub-tasks, 14 parallel-marked, all 76 criteria mapped, no phantom ids, every _Depends:_ resolves. Majors 1-6 are one branch (tooling scaffold, the two oracles, tree removal and identity erasure, guards, history tooling, evidence and landing); Majors 7-8 are the one-shot rewrite and its aftermath and cannot start until Major 6 has merged and its worktree is gone, because the quiescence gate halts while any extra worktree exists. TASKS.MD IS ITSELF TOKEN-FREE AND ADDRESS-FREE, verified by probe with a positive control against brief.md so the clean result is not a vacuous walk -- it is in scope for Req 1.3 and Req 11.1 like any other tracked file, and it carries its own naming convention. EIGHT THINGS THE TASKS PHASE CHANGED RELATIVE TO THE DESIGN, every one found by re-measuring rather than by re-reading. (1) A MISSING FOUNDATION TASK. Nothing in the design or the first draft ever CREATED the out-of-repository forbidden-string file, and six later tasks consume it. Without it every token check in the plan degrades to a skip -- the exact failure Req 11.8 exists to make visible. It is now task 2.3, ordered before 3.1 so the removed-path fragments are enumerated while the material is still in the tree, and its observable proves liveness per category rather than mere existence. (2) TWO FILES HAD NO OWNER. training-load's brief.md and requirements.md carry tokens and are absent from design.md's modified-files table, so Req 11.1 was unsatisfied for them by every task. Assigned to 3.8 under the redaction-only rule; training-load is now split file-disjoint across 3.6, 3.7 and 3.8. (3) EVERY COUNT WAS REMOVED FROM THE PLAN. requirements.md forbids resting a criterion on a count, the first draft leaked several in, and THREE HAD ALREADY DRIFTED: design says 63 token-bearing tracked files (measured 67), 13 token-bearing queue items (measured 17, 10 open and 7 closed), and this file's prior note said three token-bearing queue paths where the tree has TWO -- one open, one ALREADY IN closed/, which the draft did not account for at all since closing preserves the stem. Tasks now say 'every member the enumeration flags'. The design's 'five citing files' likewise counts the items' own self-references; the real citing set is two, one of them outside .kiro/queue/. (4) A DELETE-VERSUS-RENAME COLLISION in the sdist guard. Of five token-bearing constants, four are deleted by the re-basing, so 'delete the four value constants' plus 'rename the five token-bearing constants' double-counted the work; same overlap on the test function names. Task 4.1 now orders deletions first and renames only survivors, and distinguishes deleting the withdrawn-symbol scan WHOLE from stripping only the token assertions off the two artifact scans while keeping their structural controls. (5) A TOKEN/VALUE CONFLATION. Only src/fitdocs/plugins.py carries a token; the document-editing docstring matches ZERO on a token scan and is a value reproduction reachable only by the value matcher, so the draft's token-only observable passed straight over that edit. Observables throughout now name BOTH probes wherever both apply, and the plan states as a standing rule that an observable naming one matcher is vacuous for the other's work. (6) AN UNWRITEABLE ARTIFACT. The draft had a late task record mutation evidence 'in the commit message of the change that lands each guard', but those commits are made by earlier tasks and a later task cannot write into them. Recording moved into 4.1, 4.2 and 4.3; 6.1 now collects, confirms the evidence was gathered through `uv run pytest` rather than a bare interpreter (the stale-bytecode hazard, which is intermittent by construction and reads as a flake), and confirms each mutation redded its own assertion rather than a cascade of siblings. (7) MISSING BASELINES. The spec-status comparison for training-load and the golden-document comparison both required a 'before' that nothing captured. Task 1 now captures the spec-status baseline alongside M0, whose blob identifiers carry the golden check across the rewrite. (8) THE ADOPTION BOUNDARY LEAKED. The carry-over checklist enumerated only user-visible state, while M0, M1, the spec-status baseline, the extracted prior-map rows, the commit map, first-changed-commits, suboptimal-issues and the forbidden-string file are all consumed AFTER the old repository is destroyed and none can be regenerated. All are now on 5.5's asserted checklist, and 7.4 gates destruction of the old repository on it. ONE DECLARED CORRECTION TO THE DESIGN, stated in task 8.3 and amended in place there in the same commit rather than applied silently. design.md's ValidationGate says the M1-to-post-rewrite comparison is 'empty except for the renamed paths ... expected and enumerated in advance'. That carve-out is wrong: M1 and post-rewrite are both TIP trees, the queue renames already landed in the tree at Major 6, so no rename directive matches anything at the tip and the comparison must be EMPTY. The carve-out would have pre-authorised the one entry class that signals a stem mismatch between the tree rename and the history rename, and M1 is the only check that catches either that or a tip-level blob the sweep missed.
